messages:
alex: Heads-up: onboarding Suzaku-7B (Mistral-like) into int4 pipeline. Hitting strange emoji/tokenization + embedding projection diffs across FP16 vs int4. Repro and logs below. Anyone run into emoji-induced tokenizer drift with our quantizer shims? :confused:

alex: Minimal repro:
```bash
python export_model.py --model suzaku-7b --out suzaku_fp16.onnx --dtype fp16
python quantize.py --in suzaku_fp16.onnx --out suzaku_int4.onnx --backend awq --apply-permute
python run_infer.py --model suzaku_int4.onnx --prompt "I \u2764\ufe0f pizza" --log-tokens
```

alex: Quick logs:
```
# fp16 token ids: [11, 12879, 4, 2]
# int4 token ids: [11, 6534, 4, 2]
# embedding dot[0] diff: 0.003 -> 0.12
```

alex: Observations: int4 run emits a different token id for the heart emoji and embedding/proj dot product shifts notably. Hypothesis: the quantizer injects a permute/reshape targeting q/k/v proj axes assuming uniform head_dim; Suzaku uses heterogenous head_dims (mix of 64 and 48) and that assumption may corrupt offsets.

@tanya: paste tokenizer config + ONNX node list?

alex: tokenizer snippet: "normalizer: unicode_nfkc, pretokenizer: byte-level, policy: emoji_char_split"

alex: ONNX nodes include: "embedding.weight", "attn.q_proj", "attn.k_proj", "attn.v_proj", and a quantizer-inserted node "permute_proj_axes".

zach: permute_proj_axes is our quant shim to align Gemma/Mistral proj layout. If Suzaku has hetero head dims, a single batch reshape/transpose will mangle per-head offsets. Which exact head dims?

alex: Suzaku head dims example: [64,64,48,48,64,48,...] (legacy adapter mix). Global reshape assumes 64 everywhere.

maria: Also NFKC normalization can collapse multi-codepoint emoji sequences differently; combined with a pre-permute embedding path change, byte boundaries for tokenizer can shift, producing different token ids. So this is twofold: tokenizer edge-case + permute-induced offset bug.

ci-bot: [CI] suzaku_int4_tokenize_check failed  (tokenization mismatch). Job: https://ci.internal/3322

tanya: Can you quantize with permute disabled (--no-permute) and compare token ids and logits to isolate tokenizer vs weight-order issues?

alex: Did that: --no-permute yields matching token ids for the emoji case but logits still show small RMS difference (~0.5% next-token prob). So: (1) permute caused token id mismatches, (2) quant rounding of proj weights causes small embedding dot shifts that can affect next-token probs for sensitive tokens like multi-codepoint emoji.

zach: Action: change quantizer to emit per-head reshape+transpose when head_dims are non-uniform instead of applying a single global permute. I'll draft a fix/PR.

maria: Short-term mitigation: add a tokenizer pre-hook to canonicalize/collapse common multi-codepoint emoji sequences to a single canonical codepoint during onboarding evals. Add unit tests for these cases.

alex: Bench: 50 emoji-heavy prompts -> fp16 vs int4 (no-permute) exact match 96.8%, BLEU delta ~0.6. fp16 vs int4 (with permute) exact match 88.4%, BLEU delta ~3.9 plus token id mismatches.

tanya: When you open the PR, include minimal repro, CI link, and tag with labels onboard/suzaku and quant/permute-fix. Also add a checklist to audit model-registry for hybrid-head models.

zach: I'll add a model-registry audit step and add metadata to flag hetero head_dims so the quant path picks per-head transforms by default. Also note: after per-head permute change, validate KV cache indexing offsets (per-head transforms shift KV layout assumptions).

amend: (alex) I'll run transform_weights.py --emit-per-head and attach a small diff of proj axis order to the PR to confirm behavior matches FP16 ordering.

maria: Add tokenizer unit test for multi-codepoint emoji normalization; CI should cover both tokenization and small-batch generation checks.

ci-bot: created ticket #4782 for tokenizer unit coverage and added to the PR checklist.

tanya: Great. Ping me once PR is open and I'll coordinate a small Dedicated canary.

zach: Follow-up note in PR: include KV-cache indexing smoke tests and a short regression bench for emoji-heavy prompts.

alex: Summary in PR: root cause = global permute + hetero head_dim assumption + NFKC/byte-level tokenizer edge-case for multi-codepoint emoji. Fixes = per-head permute/reshape path, tokenizer pre-hook collapse, and CI test coverage. Opening PR now. :thumbsup:
